output.headline: Accepts a $390,000 Alameda County Probation grant for a student mentoring program at three schools
output.summary: In a memorandum of understanding (MOU), the district accepts a $390,000.00 grant from the Alameda County Probation Department for the Cross-Age Mentoring Program. High school students mentor middle school students one-on-one at Oakland High School, Westlake Middle School and Roosevelt Middle School. The term runs from June 1, 2019 to September 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $382,623.42 donation from the Chabot Elementary PTA for staff pay and hardware
output.summary: The district is accepting a $382,623.42 donation from the Anthony Chabot Elementary School PTA for Chabot Elementary School. The money supplements staff salaries and pays for hardware at the school during the 2019-2020 school year.

output.headline: Accepts a $135,402 Montclair Elementary PTA donation to fund three recess coach positions
output.summary: The district is accepting a $135,402.00 donation from the Montclair Elementary School PTA under a fiduciary agreement. The money pays for three full-time enrichment recess coach positions at Montclair Elementary School for the 2019-2020 school year.

output.headline: Ratifies a $5,000 contract with BLX Group for a review of the district's bond disclosure compliance

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The Board ratifies, or confirms after the fact, a contract with BLX Group LLC of Los Angeles to review five years of the district's continuing disclosure compliance for its outstanding bonds and write a report on what it finds. The contract runs June 20 through August 31, 2019 and may not exceed $5,000. The work began before the Board's August 14 approval.

output.headline: Ratifies the annual report of $1,963,627.06 in gifts, grants and bequests accepted in 2018-19
output.summary: The Board is asked to formally approve (ratify) the yearly report of gifts, grants and bequests the district accepted during fiscal year 2018-2019. The total listed is $1,963,627.06, with the details in Exhibit 1. Board Policy 3290 requires this report.

output.headline: Ratifies $15,670,422.57 in June 2019 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board is asked to formally approve (ratify) payroll payments made in June 2019: 896 paper payroll checks and 7,090 direct deposits. The total is $15,670,422.57, with the details in Exhibit 1. This money was already paid out.

output.headline: Ratifies $13,353,446.37 in July 2019 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board is asked to formally approve (ratify) payroll payments made in July 2019: 3,406 paper payroll checks and 4,965 direct deposits. The total is $13,353,446.37, with the details in Exhibit 1. This money was already paid out.

output.headline: Ratifies $45,822,224.24 in bills the district paid by check in June 2019
output.summary: The Board is asked to formally approve (ratify) 1,661 checks the district printed in June 2019 to pay its bills (accounts payable). The total is $45,822,224.24, with the details in Exhibit 1. This money was already paid out.

output.headline: Ratifies $19,637,630.48 in bills the district paid by check in July 2019
output.summary: The Board is asked to formally approve (ratify) 648 checks the district printed in July 2019 to pay its bills (accounts payable). The total is $19,637,630.48, with the details in Exhibit 1. This money was already paid out.

output.headline: Updates who is authorized to sign for 10 district financial accounts
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt Resolutions 1920-0007 through 1920-0016, which name the people authorized to sign on ten district financial accounts. The accounts include the cafeteria, payroll, revolving fund, workers' compensation and investment accounts. No dollar amount is attached.

output.headline: Adopts a state-team student body accounting manual and fraud prevention guide
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt Resolution No. 1920-0006, which adopts the Fiscal Crisis & Management Assistance Team's manual for handling Associated Student Body (student-run fund) accounting. The package also includes a fraud prevention guide and a desk reference. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Accepts a $250,000 City of Oakland grant for academic support at four high schools
output.summary: The district is accepting a $250,000.00 grant from the City of Oakland's Oakland Fund for Children and Youth. It pays for academic support and case management in the African American Male Achievement and Oakland Athletic League programs at Castlemont, Fremont, McClymonds and Skyline High Schools. The grant covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $50,000 from the Salesforce Foundation for Middle School Network communications
output.summary: The district is accepting $50,000.00 through the Oakland Public Education Fund, which acts as fiscal agent for the Salesforce Foundation. The money supports marketing and communication for the Middle School Network to increase funding and teacher retention. The grant period began April 1, 2019, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2020.

vendor.name: Oakland Public Education Fund (fiscal agent for the Salesforce Foundation)

output.headline: Accepts a $12,175,510 state grant to run the California State Preschool Program in 2019-20
output.summary: The district is accepting a $12,175,510.00 contract (No. CSPP-9020) from the California Department of Education to operate the California State Preschool Program through its Early Childhood Education Department. The funding covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $7,500 state grant for the Pre-Kindergarten and Family Literacy Program in 2019-20
output.summary: The district is accepting a $7,500.00 contract (No. CPKS-9001) from the California Department of Education for the Pre-Kindergarten and Family Literacy Program. The Early Childhood Education Department runs the program. The funding covers July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $2,586,937 state grant for general child care and development programs in 2019-20
output.summary: The district is accepting a $2,586,937.00 contract (No. CCTR-9010) from the California Department of Education for the state's general child care and development programs. The Early Childhood Education Department operates these programs. The funding covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $170,280 for Ninyo & Moore vapor well work at the new Fremont High School
output.summary: This amendment adds $170,280.00 to Ninyo & Moore's consulting agreement, raising the cap from $226,237.00 to $396,517.00. The added work is a technical memo for the California Department of Toxic Substances Control and the installation, sampling and destruction of vapor wells for Increments 3 and 4 of the Fremont High School new construction project. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Pays SunPower up to $95,755.20 to remove and replace the Oakland Tech solar array
output.summary: The district is hiring SunPower Corporation to remove and replace the solar array at Oakland Technical High School for no more than $95,755.20. Work starts August 15, 2019 and must finish by October 31, 2019. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $80,000 and five months for Anthonio's inspector work on Foster the Center project
output.summary: This amendment adds $80,000.00 to Anthonio, Inc.'s agreement, raising the cap from $1,185,050.00 to $1,265,050.00. The money pays for five more months of a full-time inspector of record to help commission and close out the Foster the Center project, as the Division of State Architect requires. The agreement end date moves to May 29, 2020. It is paid from Measure B bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $43,480.29 to G & G Builders' contract for Peralta Elementary play matting demolition

money.evidence: in an additional amount not to exceed $43,480.29

output.summary: This change order adds $43,480.29 to G & G Builders' contract, raising the cap from $160,946.00 to $204,426.29. The added work is extra demolition at Peralta Elementary School's play matting project: sawcutting and demolishing asphalt, pouring a concrete rat slab and patching asphalt. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Pays Applied Materials & Engineering up to $11,701 to test the Westlake Middle School turf field
output.summary: The district is hiring Applied Materials & Engineering, Inc. to provide the construction inspection and testing the Division of the State Architect requires for the new turf field at Westlake Middle School. The cost is capped at $11,701.00. Work runs from August 15, 2019 to no later than June 30, 2020, and is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Pays General Roofing up to $11,990 for temporary roof repairs at Foster Educational Leadership Complex
output.summary: The district is hiring General Roofing Company for temporary roof repairs on two stair towers at the Foster Educational Leadership Complex, for no more than $11,990.00. The work includes cleaning off loose roofing material and reconfiguring roof drains for the temporary roof. The work period began July 1, 2019, before this vote, and runs through September 30, 2019. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Pays Anthonio up to $29,040 to inspect the new turf field at Claremont Middle School
output.summary: The district is hiring Anthonio, Inc. to serve as inspector of record for the new turf field at Claremont Middle School, as the Division of State Architect requires. The inspector will also review construction documents, prepare reports, attend project meetings and give technical advice. The cost is capped at $29,040.00, and the work runs from August 15, 2019 to no later than April 3, 2020. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $156,397.94 to Redgwick's contract for the Claremont Middle School turf field
output.summary: This change order adds $156,397.94 to Redgwick Construction's contract, raising the cap from $635,957.95 to $792,355.89. The added work is demolition and installation of new turf at Claremont Middle School's playfield project. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $71,000 and a year to Ninyo & Moore's work at the LaEscuelita Educational Center
output.summary: This amendment adds $71,000.00 to Ninyo & Moore's agreement, raising the cap from $65,000.00 to $136,000.00. The added work is inspecting the accessible parts of the sub-slab ventilation system, which the California Department of Toxic Substances Control requested. The end date moves from December 31, 2018 to December 31, 2019. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $145,340 for Applied Materials & Engineering window water testing at Glenview
output.summary: This amendment adds $145,340.00 to Applied Materials & Engineering, Inc.'s agreement, raising the cap from $297,937.00 to $443,277.00. The added work is water testing of 214 windows and written reports on the results for the Glenview new construction project. The end date moves from December 31, 2019 to December 1, 2020. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Asks for a retirement-rule exemption for a recently retired teacher, under Resolution 1920-0071
output.summary: The Board approves Resolution No. 1920-0071, which seeks an exemption to the separation-from-service requirement of the California State Teachers Retirement System (CalSTRS) for a teacher who recently retired from the district. The item lists no dollar amount.

output.headline: Asks for a retirement-rule exemption for a retiring health services coordinator, under Resolution 1920-0072
output.summary: The Board approves Resolution No. 1920-0072, which seeks an exemption to the separation-from-service requirement of the California State Teachers Retirement System (CalSTRS) for a health services coordinator who is retiring from the district. The item lists no dollar amount.

output.headline: Updates the board policy on who can sign district contracts without a board vote, and the dollar limits
output.summary: The Board updates Board Policy 3312 on contracts and delegation of authority to reflect which staff positions may sign contracts on their own. The limit is either the inflation-adjusted Public Contract Code amount, currently $92,600, or $50,000 in a fiscal year cumulatively with one vendor. The item itself spends no money.

output.headline: Accepts a $70,000 grant to cover substitutes for new-teacher training days
output.summary: The district is accepting a $70,000.00 grant from the Chiling Hammer Education Fund, passed through the East Bay Community Foundation. The money pays for substitute coverage or extended contract time so staff can attend New Teacher Center professional development during the 2019-2020 school year.

vendor.name: Chiling Hammer Education Fund (via East Bay Community Foundation)

output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt Personnel Report No. 1920-0001, the district's routine list of staffing actions. The agenda text gives no details or dollar amounts.

output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt Resolution No. 1920-0128, which approves creating or revising the district's job description for Truck Driver. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Confirms the Board President's pick for the school bond oversight committee through June 2020
output.summary: The Board ratifies, or confirms, the Board President's appointment of Andre Spearman to the Measures A, B and J Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee. The appointment starts August 15, 2019 and fills the unexpired term that ends June 10, 2020.

output.headline: Reduces classified layoffs and adds classified positions for 2019-20 based on program need
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt Resolution No. 1819-0098D, which amends the 2019-2020 list of classified (non-teaching) position layoffs and additions. It reduces the number of layoffs and increases the number of authorized classified positions, based on program need. No dollar amount is stated.
